guidelineReference: Resus Council UK Paediatric Basic Life Support 2021
title: Infant cardiac arrest at a family fun day
setting: Family fun day. A frantic parent runs into the first aid post holding an 8-month-old infant in their arms. The baby is unresponsive and not breathing.
verdictExplanation: Unresponsive and not breathing normally in an infant. Paediatric cardiac arrest is a critical, time-sensitive life-threatening emergency. Sick: start CPR beginning with rescue breaths.

shared.airway: Open, requires manual positioning (neutral head position)

er.exposure: Indoors, baby is dressed in warm layers

history.history: Fell asleep in pushchair 10 minutes ago, mother checked and found him unresponsive, frantically ran to post
history.pmh: Usually fit and well, crying more regularly in the last 12 hours

followUp.question: What is your immediate resuscitation action for this infant?

options.text: Ensure neutral head position, give 5 initial rescue breaths, then perform 15:2 chest compressions to breaths
Start with 30 chest compressions, as for an adult, and tilt the head fully back
Place in the recovery position immediately and wait for the ambulance crew
Hold him upside down by the ankles and slap his back to clear the throat

followUp.explanation: Infant resuscitation begins with ensuring a neutral head position (sniffing position, not over-extended as in adults) and giving 5 initial rescue breaths. If there is no response, perform chest compressions (with two fingers or two thumbs) in a 15:2 ratio. Never hold an infant upside down or place them in recovery position if they are not breathing.

levelFlags.cfaNotes: Call 999 immediately. Resuscitate at a 15:2 ratio after 5 initial rescue breaths.
levelFlags.erNotes: Maintain airway with neutral head alignment. Check BGL and keep the infant warm. Prepare AED with paediatric attenuator/pads if available; if not, use adult pads placed front-and-back.
